title: Action routes should use Drupal routing CSRF protection
summary: Drupal secure-code documentation says CSRF protection is integrated into the routing access system and should be used for URLs that perform actions or operations and do not use a form callback.

sources.locator: Avoid cross-site request forgeries (CSRF) for routing
sources.title: Writing secure code for Drupal

drupal_core.notes: This record reflects current Drupal secure-code guidance for non-form action URLs.

actions: Use Drupal routing CSRF access protection for non-form URLs that perform actions or operations.
checks: Review custom routes that mutate state or perform operations outside form callbacks.
Confirm applicable action routes include routing-level CSRF protection.
evidence_requirements: Whether the route uses a form callback or another CSRF-protected flow
automation_hints: Future analysis can join route definitions with controller behavior to identify action routes that need CSRF access checks.

enforcement.rationale: The source supports the guidance, but enforcement requires project-specific route and behavior evidence.
